company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS at $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but quality was low — the upside was driven by tariff refunds (145 basis point tailwind to gross margins) and a non-cash LIFO impact (105 basis point tailwind), not organic strength. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. +3.1% expected, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final eight weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex at the intersection of robotics and AI-driven machine vision.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid FQ1 EPS beat at 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind. Sales disappointed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. $943.2 million expected, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed modestly to $3.88-4.03 billion from $3.93-4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged at $1.85-2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The appointment brings leadership stability to the finance function.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% vs. the 13.85% consensus estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures squeezing household budgets and keeping retail soft. Bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost-reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in participants. The results reinforce VK2735 as a credible competitor in the high-stakes obesity drug market. This is a meaningful clinical catalyst that validates the company's pipeline and could accelerate partnership or licensing interest.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector faces headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn rates, fuel costs, and inflation are pressuring consumer discretionary spending on big-ticket items. GLP-1/obesity drug sector gets a boost from Viking's positive VK2735 data. Machine vision and robotics space sees consolidation with the Cognex-RealSense deal.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, so there's no broad macro or Fed commentary today — let's go straight to the names moving before the open.

Starting with Viking Therapeutics, the standout mover. Shares are spiking in pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, with patients showing 22% weight loss. That's a strong clinical readout that puts Viking firmly in the conversation as a legitimate obesity drug competitor. Watch for sector sympathy moves and renewed deal speculation around this one.

AutoZone beat on earnings — fiscal fourth quarter EPS came in at fifty-six oh five versus the Street at fifty-four oh three — but the quality of that beat is poor. The upside was driven by tariff refunds, a 145 basis point tailwind to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO adjustment adding another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is much weaker. Domestic comps missed badly, coming in at plus 1.6% versus expectations of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did highlight improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter, which is a modest positive going into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced a roughly 500 million dollar acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI applications. RealSense is growing revenue more than 50% year-over-year in the 80 to 90 million dollar range. This is a strategic bet on robotics and AI-driven vision, and it's the kind of deal that makes sense given where industrial automation is heading.

MillerKnoll posted a solid beat — 53 cents versus 36 cents expected — and importantly, they would have beaten even without the tariff refund tailwind. However, sales fell short, down 3.3% organically, while full-year revenue guidance was trimmed slightly. Orders were up 3.5% year-over-year, which is an encouraging leading indicator.

THOR Industries missed on the bottom line, with earnings per share at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year. Management's tone was cautious, citing rates, fuel costs, and inflation squeezing consumer budgets through the key selling season. The one silver lining — North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year, suggesting demand could recover as conditions normalize.

Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November 1st. He brings a strong track record from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a routine leadership transition, not a market mover.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the high-momentum name to watch on GLP-1 enthusiasm. AutoZone's beat is unlikely to get credit given the quality issues. THOR remains in a tough macro environment for big-ticket consumer discretionary. Stay focused on the Viking move and any GLP-1 sector read-through.
